name: Sankardev Stages the Chihna Yatra
summary: Young Sankardev stages a dance-drama, the Chihna Yatra, the first of the plays and performances that grow into Ankiya Naat and the satra theatre tradition.
notes: Tradition places it around 1468 at Bordowa; no date was found in the sources checked.

name: Madhavdev Meets Sankardev
summary: At Dhuwahat, after a long debate, Madhavdev accepts Sankardev as his guru and becomes his chief disciple.
notes: 1522 is traditional; revised chronologies place the meeting in the early 1530s.

name: The Prayer House at Patbausi
summary: Settled at Patbausi near Barpeta in Koch territory, Sankardev gathers disciples around a prayer house, the pattern of the namghar and the satra.
notes: Sankardev’s flight from the Ahom kingdom is AHOM-243; his years at the Koch court are KOCH-09, 11 and 20.

name: Madhavdev Leads the Order
summary: After Sankardev’s death Madhavdev leads the Ekasarana order, while Damodardev’s followers form a separate branch, the start of the divisions (sanghati) of the movement.
notes: The branches and their dates were not checked in detail; treat as a broad outline.

name: Bhattadev Writes Assamese Prose
summary: Bhattadev renders the Bhagavata and the Gita into Assamese prose, among the earliest literary prose in a modern Indian language.

name: Aniruddhadeva Founds the Moamara Satra
summary: Aniruddhadeva founds the Moamara satra, whose disciples, many of them Morans, later rise against the Ahom state in the Moamoria rebellion.
notes: Founding date approximate. The rebellion itself is in the Ahom scenes (AHOM-203 onward).

name: A Coin at Dimapur
summary: A coin of Viravijay Narayan, probably Khorapha, struck at Dimapur, is the earliest direct evidence of the Dimasa kingdom.
notes: The Ahom attack on Dimapur in 1536 is AHOM-239 and AHOM-241.

name: A New Capital at Maibong
summary: After a 22-year interregnum following the loss of Dimapur, Nirbhaya Narayana sets up the Dimasa capital at Maibong in the hills.

name: The Dimasa Kingdom Bows to the Koch
summary: After Chilarai’s victories, the Dimasa kingdom becomes a tributary of the Koch kingdom.

name: Yasho Narayan Defeats the Jaintias at Dimarua
summary: Yasho Narayan (Satrudaman), the strongest of the Dimasa kings, defeats the Jaintias at Dimarua.
notes: The year is not given in the sources checked.

name: The Court Moves to Khaspur
summary: Koch rule at Khaspur in the Barak valley ends, the state merges with the Dimasa kingdom, and Khaspur becomes the Dimasa capital.
notes: Sources differ on when the capital moved.

name: Govindachandra Restored by the British
summary: After the Treaty of Yandabo the British restore Govindachandra to the Dimasa throne in Cachar.

name: Cachar Annexed
summary: After Govindachandra’s death (1830) the British pension off Senapati Tularam and annex his hill region (1832), then Govindachandra’s plains as Cachar district (1833).
notes: The Wikipedia article gives 1832–34 in different places.

name: The First Maha Ras Lila
summary: At Bhagyachandra’s court the first Manipuri Maha Ras Lila is performed, the beginning of the classical Manipuri dance tradition.
notes: Bhagyachandra’s flight to the Ahom court and Rajeswar Singha’s expeditions are AHOM-201 and AHOM-202.

name: Manipur under Burmese Occupation
summary: Burmese armies occupy Manipur, and many Manipuris flee to Cachar and Sylhet.

name: Gambhir Singha Retakes Manipur
summary: With British support in the first Anglo-Burmese war, Gambhir Singha drives the Burmese out and is restored as king of Manipur.

name: The Jaintia Kingdom Annexed
summary: The British annex the Jaintia kingdom, ending its rule over the plains around Jaintiapur and the Jaintia hills.

name: The Assam Tea Plant Shown to Robert Bruce
summary: Guided by Maniram Dewan, the Scottish trader Robert Bruce is shown the tea plant growing wild, used by the Singpho, in upper Assam.

name: The Assam Company
summary: The Assam Company is formed to grow tea commercially; Maniram Dewan serves it before starting his own gardens.

name: Orunodoi, the First Assamese Magazine
summary: American Baptist missionaries at Sivasagar begin Orunodoi, the first Assamese magazine.

name: Maniram Dewan and Piyali Baruah Hanged
summary: For plotting a rising in 1857 to restore Ahom rule, Maniram Dewan and Piyali Baruah are hanged at Jorhat jail.

name: Phulaguri Dhewa
summary: Peasants at Phulaguri in Nagaon rise against new taxes; police fire on the gathering, and leaders are hanged or deported.
notes: Often called the first peasant rising in Assam. Casualty figures vary by source and are not painted as fact.

name: Assamese Restored in Schools and Courts
summary: After decades of Bengali as the official language, Assamese is restored in the schools and courts of Assam, a campaign begun by Anandaram Dhekial Phukan and the missionaries.

name: Assam Becomes a Province
summary: Assam is separated from Bengal as a Chief Commissioner’s province, with Sylhet and the hill districts.

name: Jonaki
summary: Assamese students in Calcutta start the magazine Jonaki, opening the romantic age of modern Assamese literature.

name: Patharughat
summary: At Patharughat in Darrang, troops fire on peasants gathered to protest a steep rise in land revenue.
notes: The exact day is from a single source checked; casualty figures vary.

name: Eastern Bengal and Assam
summary: The partition of Bengal joins Assam with eastern Bengal in a new province, undone in 1912.

name: Gandhi in Assam
summary: Gandhi tours Assam during the Non-Cooperation movement; foreign cloth is burnt and Assamese join the national movement in numbers.

name: The Assam Women’s Association
summary: Chandraprabha Saikiani founds the Assam Pradeshik Mahila Samiti, the province’s women’s organisation.

name: Joymoti, the First Assamese Film
summary: Jyotiprasad Agarwala makes Joymoti, the first Assamese feature film, telling the story of the Ahom princess (AHOM-174, 177, 281).

name: Kanaklata at Gohpur
summary: In the Quit India movement, seventeen-year-old Kanaklata Barua leads a procession to raise the national flag at the Gohpur police station and is shot dead.

name: Bhogeswari Phukanani at Barhampur
summary: On the same day Bhogeswari Phukanani, a mother of eight, is shot while trying to raise the flag at Barhampur in Nagaon.

name: Kushal Konwar Hanged
summary: Blamed for the derailment of a military train at Sarupathar, the Gandhian Kushal Konwar is hanged at Jorhat jail.
notes: Sources differ on the date of the derailment (1942).

name: Bordoloi Refuses the Grouping
summary: Gopinath Bordoloi leads Assam’s resistance to the Cabinet Mission plan, which would have grouped Assam with Bengal.

name: The Sylhet Referendum
summary: Sylhet votes to join East Pakistan, and Assam enters independence without it.

name: The Great Earthquake
summary: One of the strongest earthquakes on record strikes Assam and Tibet, changing rivers and burying land under sand.

name: The Language Movement
summary: Assamese is made the official language of the state by the Official Language Act, after a year of agitation.

name: War Reaches Bomdila
summary: In the Sino-Indian war, Chinese forces take Bomdila; Tezpur is evacuated before the ceasefire.

name: Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed Becomes President
summary: Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed of Assam is sworn in as the fifth President of India.

name: The Assam Movement
summary: Students of AASU and others lead a six-year mass movement over immigration and the electoral rolls.
notes: Paint the mass protest; the violence of the period is not to be staged as spectacle.

name: The Assam Accord
summary: The Assam Accord is signed with the central government, ending the movement; Prafulla Kumar Mahanta becomes Chief Minister that December.

name: Farewell to Bhupen Hazarika
summary: Vast crowds in Guwahati bid farewell to the singer and filmmaker Bhupen Hazarika.
